notes: Read both units, full tribal-sovereignty and labor context, all thirteen candidates and the review. Resolved consultation as pre-regulatory tribal-land consultation, normalized rejection of a uniform partnership model, named federal-tribal-state partnerships throughout, and removed top-flight rhetoric. Rejoined tribal empowerment, human and natural resource development and the condition of avoiding undue federal interference as one governing policy approach rather than an unsupported prediction.

claims.claim_text: Where possible, consultation before new regulatory policy on tribal land should occur in Indian country with the tribal government and its members.
Republicans reject applying one uniform model to all federal-tribal-state partnerships.
Improved federal-tribal-state partnerships are expected to expand economic opportunity.
Improved federal-tribal-state partnerships are expected to deliver high-quality education to future generations.
Improved federal-tribal-state partnerships are expected to modernize the Indian Health Service and make it more responsive to local needs.
Improved federal-tribal-state partnerships are expected to build essential Indian-country infrastructure with tribal neighbors.
Republicans would use tribal self-determination and self-governance to empower American Indians to develop human and on-reservation natural resources without undue federal interference.
